objective: Audit sound mandatory-colour reachability propagation and complete the minimum-counterexample search domain through nine vertices, without assuming a directed Gallai partition.

atomic_claims.text: In a minimum-order nonempty root counterexample, the unreachable pairs are exactly the reversed edges of a spanning directed cycle.
At two distinct consecutive cycle colours, the required two-step reverse reachability must have the third colour.
Lower mandatory reachability, upper physical-domain closures, and singleton-colour propagation preserve every completion in the exact minimum-counterexample domain.
The generator program exhausted every canonical cycle word for orders three through nine with no witness; with the stated coverage argument this gives a finite root exclusion candidate through nine.

assumptions: Nonempty finite simple tournaments; arc colours in a three-element palette, not necessarily all used.
Directed monochromatic paths; different targets may use different colours.
Only finite-digraph-basic and finite-combinatorics; order minimality used explicitly.
The historical route ID is retained only as admitted provenance; partition existence is not used.
risks: Generator-side computation and proof draft have no trusted mathematical receipt.
Positive reachability is valid for minimum counterexamples only; it must not be imposed on arbitrary tournaments without the coverage lemma.
Mandatory relation edges must not be confused with physical triangle edges.
The admitted DAG still has the obsolete partition dependency; a trusted coordinator revision is needed before admission.
No conclusion at order ten or above; timeouts are not negative results.
The reproduction driver uses Python assertions; run without Python optimization and require explicit successful statuses and exit codes.
